admission.justification: Locking the three tools as the rule's wording asks was the reviewer's reading and was declined, and a later change that makes one of them commit or write knowledge has to lock it.

alternatives.option: Leave the three card writers unlocked, as the documented exception to the rule's wording.
alternatives.reason: They write onboarding cards and route indexes only, never knowledge records and never the database; they commit nothing themselves, and the closeout that would commit their edits is locked, so on an unconverted line their edits cannot land.

alternatives.option: Lock the three tools like every other write, as the rule's wording says.
alternatives.reason: Their writes cannot be committed while the closeout is locked, so the ruling records them as the exception instead.
alternatives.reconsider_when: One of the three tools starts to commit, or to write knowledge records or the database.

consequences: On an unconverted line of a locked repository the three tools still run, and their edits stay uncommitted until the line crosses through the crossing sync.
context: MIK-R24 rule 9 says that writes on an unconverted line refuse once its repository holds converted memory. Three tools write onboarding cards and route indexes into a leaf's working tree and were found unlocked in review: citation_fix, citation_migrate and route_index_refresh.
